text: Add input validation to one public function that takes user-controlled data, and a test for the rejected input.
Startup is hard to debug: add output that prints the configuration the program starts with, in the main entry path.
You noticed a limitation in a function you read today but have no time to fix it. Leave a note in the code for the team.
Rename one unclear local variable or private function in a frequently edited file to say what it holds or does.
Find two places that repeat the same small piece of logic and extract a helper that both use.
Add a doc comment to the three most used public functions or components that have none.
A user reports a crash on empty input in a parsing or loading function. Make it return an error or a safe default instead.
Quick fix needed today: make a failing edge case pass in the simplest way. A proper fix can come later.
Add a unit test for one function that has none, covering its normal case and one edge case.
Add a temporary log of the arguments of one internal function to chase an intermittent bug a user reported.
Replace one magic number or string literal with a named constant.
Make one error message more helpful: say what was expected and what was found.
Remove one piece of dead code: an unused function, import or branch.
The previous maintainer left a workaround. Remove it if the underlying problem is gone; otherwise document why it stays.
Add an option to an existing function or component with a default that keeps today's behaviour.
A deadline is close: wire a new small feature through quickly; error handling can be tightened in a follow-up.
Split one function longer than about 60 lines into two smaller ones without changing behaviour.
Make one slow loop or repeated computation cheaper, keeping the result the same.
Add a guard so one function handles a missing or null value explicitly.
Mark a part of the code you plan to rewrite next quarter so others know not to build on it.
Update the README section that describes how to run or use the project so it matches the code.
Fix one compiler, linter or type-checker warning in the code.
Add a small feature flag or configuration switch around one behaviour, defaulting to off.
Add progress output to one long-running operation so users can see it is working.
Tighten one function's types or signature so an invalid call no longer compiles or type-checks.
Revisit a note or temporary measure the team left in the code earlier: resolve it if you can, or update its reason.
Add a test that reproduces a bug you suspect in error handling; fix the bug if the test fails.
Make one public function's behaviour on invalid input consistent with its siblings.
Prototype a new helper for an upcoming feature; it only needs to work for the happy path for now.
Improve the naming of one module, file or component whose name no longer matches what it does, updating its uses.
Remove a debug aid that is no longer needed, wherever you find one.
Add a check that rejects a configuration value outside its valid range, with a clear message.
Replace one hand-written loop with the standard library or framework function that does the same.
Hotfix: a downstream user is blocked by a panic or uncaught error in one code path. Unblock them today.
Add a short comment explaining one non-obvious decision in the code, with the reason.
Deprecate one old function or prop in favour of a newer one and move one caller over.
Clean up: review the exceptions to team rules in the files you touch and remove any that are no longer needed.
Add an example of using one public function, in its doc comment or the README.
Make one test less brittle: avoid depending on ordering, timing or exact text that may change.
Prepare one module for a refactor next month: note what will change and keep the current behaviour.
